scenarios.title: What breaks when the business does
scenarios.intro: Each scenario rebuilds this one business in memory under a disaster chosen from a fixed menu. Nothing is typed in, and the disaster is the only difference from the baseline.
scenarios.resultTitle: Chosen scenario next to the baseline
scenarios.receiptNote: Scenario objects are built in memory, so the verify command in the scope above does not apply to them. They are checked by their integrity hash and by scenarios.run --check (DECISIONS 41).
findings: Collapses are declined by the affordability gate, not by the risk model.
PD does not rise with the disaster, so the risk model is not a stress detector.
A shock in the final three weeks is invisible to the forecast, which averages over a longer period.
The anomaly lens always returns its cap, even in the calm scenario, so its list is a review queue and not an alarm.
scenarios.caveat: Each scenario is a single business (N = 1). These are demonstrations, not estimates.

landing.title: Know where your business is heading, and why.
landing.lead: Ma'al reads a small business's cash flow through four lenses: credit, Sharia screen, zakat and forecast. Every result carries a receipt anyone can re-run. This demo runs on synthetic data.
landing.tryIntro: Five synthetic businesses, one for each state the API returns. Each card reads its decision and profile status from the API.
landing.howTitle: From transactions to a decision you can check

steps.title: Transactions
steps.text: Ninety days or more of bank and POS activity for one business.

steps.title: Profile
steps.text: Behavioural features computed once, each with its reason when missing.

steps.title: Four lenses
steps.text: Credit, Sharia screen, zakat and forecast, plus a review queue.

steps.title: Verdict and receipt
steps.text: A plain answer, with a receipt of hashes anyone can re-run.

lensText.credit: Approve, decline or set conditions, with the factors that pushed each way. Markup is fixed at signing; late payments go to charity.
lensText.sharia: A rule-based screen that says plainly it is pending Sharia-advisor confirmation, and shows every rule it checked.
lensText.zakat: From zakatable assets to the amount due, step by step, with the hawl and the nisab marked.
lensText.forecast: Projected runway against the cash floor, next to a naive baseline so the model has to earn its place.

landing.factsNote: Counts of what the demo contains, not performance claims.
landing.whyTitle: Most lenders hide the model or reduce it to a score. Ma'al shows its work.

why.title: A receipt on every decision
why.text: Each result carries the hashes of its config, model, data and code. Re-run it with the same inputs and the output hash must match.

why.title: Sharia-first, and honest about it
why.text: The screen is labelled as rule-based until a Sharia advisor confirms the rule table. Markup never changes after signing.

why.title: Zakat you can follow
why.text: The amount is built in front of you from the balance sheet, with a plate showing whether the gold price behind the nisab has been verified.

why.title: Model numbers on the receipt
why.text: The credit model's cross-validated AUC and its ceiling are printed on every compliance view, straight from the receipt.

faq.a: No. Ma'al shows the output of a demo credit lens on synthetic data. It is not an offer from any bank, and the markup is not an APR.

faq.q: Is the Sharia screen a religious ruling?
faq.a: No. It applies a rule table and says so on every page until a Sharia advisor confirms that table.
No. Every business in the demo is synthetic. A real deployment would need a PDPL notice, per-owner access and SAMA Open Banking consent.

faq.q: What does a receipt let me do?
faq.a: It lists what produced the result, so anyone with the repository can re-run the decision and check that the output hash matches.
